Paragraph: In Bhagavad Gita Chapter 5, Verse 22, Krishna teaches Arjuna: 'Pleasures derived from contact with sensory objects are sources of misery, for they have a beginning and an end, O son of Kunti. A wise person does not delight in them.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Dependence on external validation and sensory pleasures, leading to anxiety and dissatisfaction.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna points out the transient nature of external pleasures, urging Arjuna to seek joy within rather than in temporary external conditions.
Outcome/Resolution: Reducing reliance on external pleasures fosters lasting peace and protects against disappointment.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Bhoga-Duhkha (Understanding that sensory indulgence leads to sorrow)
Antar-Sukha (Inner joy independent of external objects)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Sensory pleasures are short-lived; true happiness is found by going inward.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Reflects psychological principles regarding hedonic adaptation and the limits of external gratification.
